message.content: In lions, one of the most well‑known dominant traits is the **presence of a mane** in males. The genetic factor that controls mane development is inherited in a dominant fashion—if a male lion carries the allele for mane growth, it will express the trait, whereas females (who are typically smaller and lack a mane) do not carry the same dominant allele. This dominant trait is what gives male lions their distinctive, mane‑covered appearance.
